title: yian.message.v1
description: One yian message: yian's own message records (run logs, session transcripts, model_attempt.partial, conformance scripts). yian reads them strictly and refuses an unknown key or part type; later versions add keys and part types, so a newer record fails an older yian. An optional key is left out, never null. Payloads (provider_payload, tool-call arguments) are opaque JSON whose numbers are finite and whose ints have any size. In yian's codec form (run logs, frames), a payload object shaped like {"$float": "inf"} or {"$float": "-inf"}, or whose only key is $record, is written as {"$record": <object>}; message numbers are never infinite.

protocol.description: The protocol id of the adapter that produced the message, e.g. openai_responses or catalog:<provider>. Every provider payload in the message belongs to it.

part.description: One part of a message, told apart by its type.

text.description: Text the model wrote or the user sent.

media.description: An image or file, given inline as base64 data or by url; exactly one of the two.

tool_call.description: A tool call the model asked for, with arguments, raw_arguments or both. By adapter convention, arguments is left out exactly when the raw text failed to parse.

id.description: The call id that the tool result answers.

raw_arguments.description: The arguments text as the model sent it.

tool_result.description: The result of a tool call, sent back to the model.

call_id.description: The id of the call this answers.

is_error.description: Whether the tool failed; left out when false.

reasoning.description: The model's reasoning text, or a summary of it; it may be empty.

refusal.description: The model's refusal to answer, kept apart from its text; it may be empty.

provider_payload.description: Opaque provider data, kept untouched; usually a replay record ($defs/replay_record).

replay_record.description: Provider data an adapter sends back on a later turn. kind is the protocol id, v the version (1), provider and model the ones the record came from, and account, when present, a non-secret hash of the account the record is bound to; the other keys are the protocol's fields. A new field is additive; a changed meaning bumps v. A record that doesn't match the request is left out of it, never an error.
